utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the court. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Aditya Menon and Daryl Mundis for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my colleagues from the OTP, to everyone in and around the courtroom. I am Vasvija Vidovic, with Mr. Nicholas Robson, representing General Delic, with legal assistant, Lejla Gluhic, and today helped with our intern, Claire Bonnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Good morning, Mr. Ribo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I know you must be knowing this by now, but it's still my duty to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony, to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know, I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps if the usher could assist by lower the mirror on the ELMO, that might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For you to see Mr. Ribo?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ribo.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My name is Daryl Mundis. I represent the Prosecution in this case. I'm going to be asking you some questions. You, sir, remember testifying here at the Tribunal in the Hadzihasanovic case and Kubura case?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That was, perhaps if you don't recall, on the 28th of October, 2004.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but I remember that I did testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on that day, I also asked you some questions. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I really didn't remember your face.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's fine. Let me just ask you some preliminary questions about testifying in the Hadzihasanovic case. You remember that, just like in this case, you took a solemn declaration to tell the whole truth before you testified?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at that point in time, when you testified in the Hadzihasanovic case, you answered all the questions truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say, Mr. Ribo, that when you testified in that trial more than three years ago, that your memory of the events during the war was better than it is today?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, at the time, Mr. Ribo, you testified in the Hadzihasanovic case, if I remember correctly, you told us that you were a brigadier in the Army of BiH.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a colonel in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; but in the Army of the Federation, I was a brigadier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And let me ask you, sir, do you still hold that position today or are you currently retired?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am retired now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which position are we referring to, the colonel position in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina or brigadier in the Army of the Federation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I can ask some questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you just tell us, sir, the difference between the Army of BiH and the Army of the Federation of BiH?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was a wartime organisation in which I was a colonel. After the signing of the Dayton Accords, the Army of the Federation was formed, composed of Croats and Bosniaks, and then it was the Army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, in effect, what happened was the Army of BiH became the Army of the Federation of BiH, with the HVO joining the Armija?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during the war, you were a colonel in the ABiH; and after the war, you were a brigadier in the Federation -- in the Army of the Federation of BiH?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sometime between the time when you testified in Hadzihasanovic on 28 October 2004 and today, you retired from the Army of the Federation of BiH?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I retired from the Ministry of Defence of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When did you retire, Mr. Ribo?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a year and a half ago, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me go back, sir, to the time period 1994 and 1995. Can you just remind us of what position you held within the 3rd Corps in 1994 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 1994, I was the chief of the armoured mechanised units at the Staff of the 3rd Corps. In 1995, I was the chief of the section for operations and training. After that, after the signing of the day Dayton Accords, I was the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to focus your attention for a few moments on 1995, at which point in time you were the chief of the section for operations and training within the 3rd Corps. Can you tell us, Mr. Ribo, a little bit about what that job entailed and what your responsibilities were?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like I've been testifying over the past few days, I was responsible for planning, drafting of monthly and annual plans, analysis of the plans, drafting combat documentation, drawing topographical maps, and drafting other kinds of combat documents like orders, different record books. I was also entrusted with combat training and education, so I was responsible for training. Some other matters also I will probably remember in the course of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And as part of your responsibilities that you've just outlined, you would need to know about the units that were part of the 3rd Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And part of that information that you would require to fulfill your duties would be to know which lower-level units were subordinated to mid-level units within the corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I really don't understand this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me phrase it a different way. In 1995, the corps had divisions; correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And as part of fulfilling the duties you had, as chief of operations and training, you would need to know which brigades were in which division?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, I didn't have to know, but I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you to clarify that, because when you say you didn't have to know, why wouldn't you have to know that if you were in charge of planning? Wouldn't you have to know which brigades were in which divisions?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Corps Command didn't order tasks to lower-ranking units, ones that were part of divisions. We were issuing assignments to divisions and not to its brigades. We were not responsible for issuing assignments to brigades, because that would violate the chain of command. We would issue orders first to the subordinate units of the corps. If that happened to be a division, then we would be issuing assignments to a division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I understand. I understand the differentiation that you're making. I'm not talking about issuing orders to the brigade, because clearly that would violate the principles of unity of command. What I'm talking about is you simply knowing, in your position, which brigades were in which divisions.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, in order to fulfill your duties and responsibilities, you would have to know the locations, the areas of responsibility, of all of the lower-level units of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have to know the areas of responsibility. I had to know the area of responsibility of the 35th Division, the 37th Division, for example, but I did not have to know the area of responsibility of their subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you know that information, whether you had to know it or not? Did you know it in 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's go back now, sir, to the period 1992, when you were the chief of the Travnik Territorial Defence Staff. I'm particularly interested in some of the testimony that you gave both this week and also in the Hadzihasanovic trial concerning the Patriotic League, so I'd like you to focus your attention on the Patriotic League for a moment. You told us two days ago that the Territorial Defence was not accepted by the Patriotic League. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Because I believe you also told us - and this is reflected on page 7003, lines 17 to 22 of yesterday's transcript - that the Patriotic League was on the right flank of units within your AOR in Gluha Bukovica. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, in 1992, within the area of responsibility of the Travnik Territorial Defence Staff, the Patriotic League was on the front lines to the right-hand side of your units, but within your AOR?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the Patriotic League that came from Zenica. That was the 314th Brigade, with the Commander Midhat Puric. He and his Patriotic League unit was in that sector of the front, but not constantly, only from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what the relationship was? Because your answer spoke about both the Patriotic League and the 314th Brigade. Was the 314th Brigade formed out of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that it was -- well, it was a unit that was in Zenica, and the smaller units of the Patriotic League joined together to form it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, in 1992, when the Patriotic League was on the right wing or right flank of units within your AOR, what the Patriotic League was doing?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like all the other units, it was executing combat assignments in that part. It's a small section of the front that the Patriotic League held. It had 40 or 50 people, and it couldn't really hold any particular positions. It was a very small section, but I have to say that it was not logistically connected to my TO Staff. I did not provide weapons to them. They simply came and carried out combat tasks, held defence positions, without my logistical support.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say they carried out combat tasks and held defence positions, the armed force that they were engaging in combat against or holding defence positions against was the VRS?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They just held the lines of defence. They didn't participate in active combat. But that is correct, they were facing the lines of the Army of Republika Srpska on their lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which was the same army that you were defending against with the Territorial Staff of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this, because you've mentioned logistics, with respect to the Patriotic League: Where was the Patriotic League getting its logistical support from?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. They did not depend, in the logistical sense, on my units or on my staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, you are aware, however, that the Patriotic League was receiving financial support from outside Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To an extent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, testifying about the Patriotic League receiving 40.000 German marks from Turkish journalists?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you were actually called or summoned to be a witness to this transaction, were you not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When was that, approximately?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was maybe in August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about the circumstances surrounding that, your recollection of what happened, concerning this financial transaction?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Patriotic League commander of this small unit asked me to be there as a witness when the journalists handed this money to him. I agreed simply to be a witness, and I know that Midhat Puric did receive this money. He was the commander of the unit. And I know that definitely, because I saw that man after that, that he was captured when he still had the 40.000 marks on him, by the HVO. He was at the Novi Travnik camp called "Kaci," and this money was confiscated from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, when you talk about this person being captured with the 40.000 marks at Kaci, you're referring to Midhat Puric?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, I am thinking of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn now, Mr. Ribo, to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, we didn't quite finish the story of the relations between the Patriotic League and the 314th Brigade. I think the witness said that smaller units of the Patriotic League somehow broke away from that league and joined in or formed the 314th Brigade. Now, this may be of some significance, and I'd like you to elicit from the witness a little bit of information about what happened, and particularly if the Patriotic League continued to exist after the formation of the 314th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, let me ask you this: For how long did the Patriotic League exist as a military formation or with military capabilities?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it existed up until the forming of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I think up to June or July. At least in my Travnik area, the Patriotic League disbanded in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say "June or July," what year are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I take it, then, you told us Midhat Puric, who had been the commander of the Patriotic League forces, became the commander of the 314th Mountain Brigade of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. He was not the commander of the 314th. He did not join the 314th. Midhat Puric did not join the 314th. After the brigade was formed, he personally did not become a member of the 314th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, what position, if any, Midhat Puric held after the Patriotic League was disbanded?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know what his function was or in which unit he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing Midhat Puric after the Patriotic League was disbanded?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see Midhat Puric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the Patriotic League forces that you've been talking about, what geographic area were they operating in?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're thinking about the Travnik Municipality, I've already said that this was in the Gluha Bukovica sector, which is an area called "Neokren."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after the 314th Mountain Brigade was formed, what geographic area was it responsible for?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot say where the 314th Brigade was located. I know it was a manoeuvre unit. It was not in the area of Zenica. There was no aggressor in Zenica. So it was engaged on different assignments within the 3rd Corps area of responsibility, but I don't know the locations that it actually was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we've taken that about as far as we can, and I'll move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I'd now like to turn your attention to the Muslim Forces or the Muslimanske Snage. A few days ago, you were shown a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 103. Perhaps we can pull that up for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, do you see this document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't see the whole document, but I see the heading on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we can just zoom out so the witness can see the entire first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, you were asked some questions about this document two days ago. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you were asked a question by my learned colleague, Mrs. Vidovic, and this is reflected on page 6997, lines 7 through 9: "Can you tell us whether this document ever reached your TO Staff?" And your answer was: "No, never." And my first question to you, Mr. Ribo, is: Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And are you absolutely sure that this document never reached your TO Staff?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm quite sure I've never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I ask you that, sir, because you were shown the same document in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura trial. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, again, on the 28th of October, 2004, the transcript in that case, page 10865, Judge Swart, one of the Judges in that trial, asked you about this document, and he said to you: "Did you ever receive the document?" And the transcript records the following answer: "I may have. I'm not sure. There are many bodies within my command. It could have been sent to one of those bodies. Those bodies were independent. Logistics people could write certain instructions, orders, et cetera. Even the chief of security could do that, especially the officer in charge of personnel could draft such documents, affix stamps, request certain data. So this list didn't necessarily pass through my hands."

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just said that I personally never saw this list. I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. But the question, sir, is whether -- the question that Mrs. Vidovic asked was: "Can you tell us whether this document ever reached your TO Staff?" And you said: "No, never." And so what I'm asking you, in light of what you've told us about this document, concerns whether the document reached the TO Staff.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember such a document passing through my hands or reaching me. I don't know -- or rather, I can't see, from this list, why it was requested, what the purpose of the list was. And even if it was sought by one of the organs of my command, I really don't know what they would do with such a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I understand. I understand what you're saying, Mr. Ribo, but I just -- what I'm trying to get from you, sir, is whether you are in a position to categorically state that this document never reached the TO Staff, or it's possible it reached the TO Staff but it didn't reach your hands, personally.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, whatever my Command sought in writing had to have my signature; and whatever arrived in writing, I had to place my initials on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Ribo, it's clear from the document it makes no reference that it's being sent in response to a request from the TO Staff. The question is whether you're in a position to state categorically that this document was never received by the TO Staff in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can state with certainty that it never reached my staff, because I had daily briefings with my assistants. Had any of my assistants asked this, he would have had to tell me why, what he was intending to do with the list, and so on and so forth. This list means nothing. When I was analysing the document, I saw that it differed considerably from other documents that we had concerning the Muslim Forces. I don't know why or what the contents of the list are. It really is not clear to me at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you explain to us, Mr. Ribo, in light of this answer, where you state with certainty that it never reached your staff, can you explain to us why, more than three years ago when Judge Swart showed you this document and asked you, "Did you ever see the document," you answered, "I may have. I'm not sure"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, really. I don't remember the answer. You say that that was my statement. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, at any point in time in 1992, when you were serving as the chief of the Territorial Defence Staff in Travnik, receiving any documents from the Muslimanske Snage, Travnik?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, again, a few days ago, you testified that there were no foreign fighters in the Muslim Forces. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You also told us, sir - and this is on 4 March, page 6997, lines 19 through 22 of the transcript - that you know Mr. Makteuf, who's listed as number 2 on this document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the name of the individual mentioned under number 2 on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How do you know Mr. Makteuf or how are you familiar with his name?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because my people at the Staff -- or rather, sometime on the 25th of February, I arrived in Travnik after having been away from Travnik for a long time. My colleagues from the Staff were aware of this individual, Makteuf; and when I asked about him, they told me that he had lived in Travnik some ten to 15 years before the war as a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You also, two days ago when asked about this, mentioned that Mr. Makteuf lived in Travnik as a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I highlight that, sir, because Mr. Makteuf is an Iraqi who acquired Bosnian citizenship. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Why do you -- why have you, on two separate occasions, then, indicated or stressed that he was a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because my men from the Staff told me, when I asked them about this individual after having testified in Hadzihasanovic and Kubara, that this was an individual who had lived in Bosnia-Herzegovina for a long time, some 15 years in Travnik, and that he was a Bosnian citizen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Have you ever met Mr. Makteuf?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I never got to know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Two days ago, you were also shown a video, which is Exhibit 55, and you made some comments about this video. And perhaps, out of an abundance of caution and to refresh your memory, we should take a quick look at this video once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that we now play Exhibit 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, do you remember seeing this videotape?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, what this videotape depicts?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that the two individuals are holding a speech. I suppose that this is Plava Voda or the area below the Medresa, since you can see the cemetery in the background.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say Plava Voda or the area below the Medresa, this is Travnik?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct, Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on the 4th of March, just two days ago, at page 6993, lines 16 through 21, in response to a question concerning this tape, you answered: "I think that this was the celebration or the ceremony, the formal ceremony of the formation of this force, the Muslim Armed Forces, and it is the oath-swearing ceremony." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This person holding the megaphone that you see on your screen immediately in front of you, which is at 12.24 on Exhibit 55, that's Abdul Aziz, is it not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that individual. I've never seen him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know where this person is from, Abdul Aziz?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness said that he didn't know the individual or that he had heard -- that he hadn't heard of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: He said, "I don't know the individual. I never seen him before." That doesn't preclude him knowing something about him from another source. But the question's been answered, anyway, and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll turn now to a different subtopic concerning the Muslim Forces, Mr. Ribo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall who the first commander of the Muslim Forces was?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was Asim Koricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after the 3rd Corps was established and its brigades were formed, Asim Koricic became the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And Mr. Koricic was later replaced as the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade commander by his deputy Amir Kubura; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that that was the case, but I don't know what the personnel developments were. There were several commanders of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, after Amir Kubura, the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, was Halil Brzina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Halil Brzina became the commander toward the end of the war, I mean the commander of the brigade. His predecessor, as far as I remember, was Patkovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name--

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We're getting there, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: After Amir Kubura, the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was Serif Patkovic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes, I believe it was Patkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after Serif Patkovic, the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was Halil Brzina?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, because I know for a fact that Patkovic, as the commander of the 7th, had been sent for medical treatment in Germany from the positions in Zenica, and Brzina was appointed in his stead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after the 3rd Corps was established and its brigades were formed, many of the soldiers who had been with the Travnik Muslimanske Snage were added to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them, of course. As far as I know, some of them became members -- became members of the 1st Battalion of the 7th. The others became members of the 306th, 312th, 325th, 308th, 317th. For the most part, they joined the units from the areas where they actually originally came from, where they hailed from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, the question was "many of the soldiers," not "all of the soldiers," "many of the soldiers who joined the Travnik Muslimanske Snage were added to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade." Would you agree or disagree with the characterization "many"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I believe that most of them became members of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, then, most of the members of the Travnik Muslimanske Snage became members of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade after that brigade was established?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, after it was established, was based in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the area of deployment of the 7th Muslim, most probably because I wasn't in Travnik at the time when the 7th Muslim Brigade was set up. I really don't know their areas of deployment or where they were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would -- perhaps if we can get Exhibit 1127 ready to play.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I want to just go back now for one brief second, sir, to Mr. Puric that we've talked about earlier this morning. I'm going to show you Exhibit 1127, and I'm going to ask you if you see Mr. Puric on this videotape. And if you do, tell us to stop and we'll stop the videotape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, if you see Mr. Puric?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we rewind the footage a bit? It seems to me that the bearded individual is Midhat Puric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that is, sir, the person wearing what appears to be a blue beret; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do have some still captures from this videotape. Perhaps if I can distribute these and I just have the witness identify the person he's identified as Mr. Puric. Then we'd ask that that be admitted as a court exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you could please just hold on a minute, Mr. Ribo, while these are being distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: One there, and if the usher could assist with putting that photo on the ELMO, please. Now, if the witness could be handed just a marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask you, sir, on the hard copy, not on the computer screen, on the hard copy, if you could please circle the person that you've identified as Midhat Puric.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if you could then just write on there, please, "Puric."

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I suggest you add "Midhat" as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'd ask that that be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The still photograph is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number. What did it come as, a still photograph of Mr. Puric?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will become Exhibit 1191.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could now have Exhibit 92. That document can be removed, Mr. Usher. Thank you. If we could have Exhibit 92 pulled up, please, and specifically page 11 of Exhibit 92. That's fine. I also have a hard copy of this page which may be of assistance to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise any of the persons on this photograph that's on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise Nusret Avdibegovic, the Travnik Mufti, and I recognise Sakib Mahmuljin, the commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, if perhaps the usher could assist with then pen and placing this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please, sir, write or draw an arrow to the person you've identified as Nusret Avdibegovic and write his name in the white margin on the outside of the photo?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And he's the Travnik Mufti; is that correct? You don't need to write that, Mr. Ribo. And Sakib Mahmuljin, can you do the same thing, write his name on the right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, the person between the mufti and General Mahmuljin, do you know who that is, the person in the military uniform with the beard?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at the person very closely, the person behind General Mahmuljin and the person that you don't know the identity of, the person in the -- with the beard and the uniform. Do you see the man in a light-coloured shirt who also has a beard, sitting to the right behind General Mahmuljin?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who is that person?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We would ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Isn't that Exhibit 92, page 11?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You want this page to be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This page with the markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This page of Exhibit 92 is entered into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit 1192.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, yesterday or the day before, you mentioned the name of Adil Lozo. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I believe that the person in the light-coloured shirt is Adil Lozo, but I couldn't see his forehead. There's an obstacle in the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is it possible to have that photo returned to the witness? Perhaps if we could put it back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is that person, sir, sitting behind Mr. Mahmuljin, in the light-coloured shirt with the trimmed beard, Adil Lozo?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: His forehead is obscured. The person does look like him very much, but I can't say for a fact that it is him, for not seeing the upper part of his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, I am aware that this document's already been admitted, and I don't believe we should make any further markings on it; but for the record, I believe it's clear enough, what the witness has just testified about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you told us, I believe it was two days ago, that Mr. Lozo was an attorney and that he was --

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- and that he was involved with the Patriotic League. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What was his function in the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim with certainty that he was connected with the Patriotic League, but he socialised with Aganovic, who was the commander of the Sector Staff of the Patriotic League in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you tell us "Aganovic," can you tell us the first name of this person Aganovic that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was mentioning Aganovic yesterday, and today I can't recall his first name. Zihnija Aganovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Zihnija Aganovic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That exhibit can be withdrawn. I ask that we now pull up P01314, P01314.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, Mr. Ribo, do you recall or can you tell us what position you held in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 301st Mechanised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In the period of June 1993, would it be fair to say that there were periodic meetings at the 3rd Corps Command, which was at that point in time commanded by General Enver Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would be fair to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at this periodic meetings, was it the normal routine that the various brigade commanders would report on what was happening in their AORs or with respect to the combat taskings or combat situation in their AORs?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If they were briefings, then the commanders briefed the corps commander on these matters, but it was quite possible that other matters were discussed, in addition to the briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you just perhaps explain to us a little bit about how these briefings went? I mean, was it the situation where General Hadzihasanovic would simply go around the room and each brigade commander would give a brief oral report or an update; is that how these worked?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, that's the way it went, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if the English version of this document could be scrolled to the very bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I draw your attention to the document that you see on the screen on the left-hand side. This is a page, sir, from the 3rd Corps war diary of 23 June 1993, concerning a meeting at Biljesevo. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it, but I don't see that it's a war diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I do have the original here, and if I can just have one moment. I would ask, perhaps with the assistance of the usher, that this be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you're looking for the actual page on the screen, you'll note that stamped on the top of each page is an eight-digit number. Do you see those numbers that have been stamped?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just so you understand, those numbers are put on documents by the Evidence Unit here at the Tribunal. Those are not stamp numbers that would have been put on by the 3rd Corps. If you go, sir, to the page that's stamped -- the last four digits are stamped "4198," that will take you to the pages that we have on the screen in front of us. "4198" stamped on the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While you're paging, Mr. Ribo, are you satisfied that that is the war diary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a book, so it's a PTT post office book and it's not paginated, so it's a little bit strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Does it appear to be the war diary of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that it's a 3rd Corps war diary. There's no stamp, it's not certified, it's not paginated. It's not the usual book that we would use for the war diaries, so I really don't know. I would have difficulty in asserting that this was a war diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me -- let me ask you a couple of additional questions, then, because we've seen several other war diaries. When you say, "It's not the usual book that we would use for the war diaries," what does the usual book that you would use for the war diaries look like?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The columns are different, the ones that are printed at the top of the page. The actual columns are not the same. This is a book with columns used by a post office, where you enter records of post sent out. It looks more like some sort of a court register or book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, yesterday you looked at two other diaries or books. I have here, for example, Exhibit 394, which is a pink notebook. Is this what a usual war diary would look like?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The columns are very important and the name put in the column, and here they are quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, similarly, Exhibit 511, which I'm holding up and you looked at yesterday, is this a usual war diary book, this notebook?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, judging by the war diaries that were maintained by my department, that is correct. You can see that the columns required are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And these two exhibits, 394 and 511 again that I'm holding up, where did you go to get these? Were these issued by the army?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We would just buy the notebooks on the market, and you can see that the columns were entered by hand. They were not printed. They were just purchased in the shops, and then we would actually format the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And isn't it true, Mr. Ribo, that during the war, and particularly in the summer of 1993, that you were forced to get these books wherever you could get them, the blank books?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were places in companies where we could find notebooks. It wasn't a problem, as far as notebooks and paper are concerned. Really, it wasn't a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But what I'm saying is there wasn't a standard distribution system set up for blank war diaries or notebooks. You were simply getting them wherever you could find them.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this book that you have in front of you, you told us, you think comes from the post office, based on the printed headings on each of the top of the pages?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's turn to this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Ribo. When you nod, we can see that you are agreeing, but unfortunately the transcript doesn't show that you have nodded. So if you could please say something to say whether you're agreeing with what is being said or disagreeing with it, then it gets recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I agree with what the Prosecutor said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn, then, to this page 4198; and if it would be easier for you in the hard copy, sir, by all means look at that. But, otherwise, it is visible on the computer screen, page 4198.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While Mr. Mundis is looking at his pages, Mr. Ribo, can I ask you a question? Is it fair to say that at page 4198, the handwritten entries are made not according to the columns printed on that book? The entries are just in manuscript, going across the entire page, so that, in fact --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, at the top of the page - and, again, this is the very bottom of the page in the English translation - but at the top of the page in the original, it indicates that it's referring to a meeting between the officers of the 3rd Corps, Biljesevo, 23 June 1993, and then a list of attendees? Is that what this document indicates, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, to me the two pages we have on the screen do not look the same, and I wonder if there is some sort of a discrepancy between the English and the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The English translation, Your Honour, simply runs from the entire document. What we have here, as a proposed exhibit, is an excerpt from the diary. So if the witness were to turn to the preceding page, in the original you would see the information that's contained at the top of the page on the English translation. Is that clear, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, let me return to the question. Based on what's written in this document, this page purports to reflect a meeting between the officers of the 3rd Corps, on 23 June 1993, in Biljesevo, and contains a list of persons attending that meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that that is written there, but I don't know if it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, your name appears on that list, does it not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name does appear, but I was not at this meeting. I've never been to Biljesevo, ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, okay. Are you absolutely sure about that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm 100 per cent sure. Perhaps it was my chief of staff of the brigade that was present, because I was really not there. I have never -- I've never been to Biljesevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you then turn, sir, to the page, again looking at the stamped numbers, 4204, 4204.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in the English, this would be page 5. It's about the top third in the English. It's right in the middle in the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, the entry: "301 Mechanised Brigade-Ribo, Haso"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Because this document would purport to indicate or to specify what you were reporting at this meeting in Biljesevo; a reference to a field gun, references to Maglaj, Tarcin, problems with ammunition, and an indication that: "We have no other problems."

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm saying that in 1993, I was never in Biljesevo; and, I don't know, it's possible that my chief of staff was there, but I don't recall actually sending my chief of staff to a briefing like this, really. I only heard of Biljesevo when I became the chief of the department for planning of combat operations when a training centre was located there. But I've never heard of it before and I've never been there, so I really don't know what location -- where this meeting was held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's just get clarity. Earlier, you said you've never been to Biljesevo, ever. Now you're saying in 1993. Which is the correct position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1993, the year to which this document refers that I have in front of you, in 1993 I never was in Biljesevo. I'd never been to Biljesevo before as a civilian, as a citizen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you have been in Biljesevo at some other time outside 1993 in your life?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, that is correct. I did go to Biljesevo after 1993. In 1995, I was there, I went there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you're chief of staff attended the meeting, would he mention your name as present or would he mention himself as present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know if anyone from my brigade actually attended this meeting. I really don't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the practice, to your knowledge, where somebody went on behalf of another person? Would he then say the other person whom he represents is attending the meeting or would he say he or she, himself, is attending the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know what the practice was. It's possible that this record was not taken by experienced officers and they don't know all the senior officers, but I really did not attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're speculating now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not speculating. It's just that I was not at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness specifically is saying, "I was not present at that meeting"; and with the greatest possible respect and consideration, I don't see how that could be speculation. And another thing, Your Honours, since I'm already on my feet. I just would like to draw attention that -- to the fact that my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, is saying or is suggesting that Mr. Ribo spoke or said something there. Can we please read exactly what is written here, and are there any indications at all that Mr. Ribo said anything or does it actually say something else here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will do that in due course. Let me just respond to what you said about me. I am not, by any means, disputing what Mr. Ribo is saying, that he was not there, but I don't know how you can deny that it is speculation to suggest or for a person who was not present to suggest that maybe - he actually says "maybe" - it was written by inexperienced people. That's speculation, isn't that? Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time. Is this not when we normally have our first break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at quarter after 11.00. Quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, earlier this morning, before I showed you this diary or this book, I asked you a series of questions about the normal routine that was undertaken at corps -- these periodic corps meetings. Do you remember me asking you about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the normal procedure was that the corps commander would chair the meeting, the brigade commanders would report about what was going on in their area of responsibility and highlight any problems that they might have encountered; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, but not all the commanders were always present, as a rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's clear. Now, just so that we're absolutely certain about one thing here, in the 301st Mechanised Brigade, the brigade that you commanded in 1993, or at least the middle of 1993, you were the only person named "Haso Ribo" in that brigade?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, if we could please - and, again, I still have the original, if we'd like to look at that - but I would ask if we could go back to the preceding page in both the Bosnian and the English on the screen. And if the witness would like to see the book, we can do that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would you prefer to see this version, sir, or would you like to look at it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And for the record, we're looking now at the Bosnian page bearing ERN number 0181 -- no. I need to go back to the page immediately before the last one. It should end in "41" -- or "4203." 0181-4203. Then immediately -- yeah. Then if we can go to the bottom on the English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, if you look at this page bearing the number "4203" at the top, halfway down there's a reference to: "7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, NS," or chief of staff, "Kubura." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask you if you could please read that entry to yourself, continuing on to the top of the following page?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, similarly, this goes on to the following page in English, once everyone's had a chance to read it. If we could please go to the next page in English and in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Have you finished reading this, Mr. Ribo?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I know, sir, that you've already told us that, in 1993, you were never in Biljesevo. My question to you is: In light of the fact that it might be possible that this meeting did not occur in Biljesevo, were you present at this meeting where Mr. Kubura discussed foreign nationals and apparently spoke about continuing to hire them because they receive ammunition?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I wasn't. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you ever present, sir, in the first half of 1993, at meetings of the 3rd Corps where the -- where there was a discussion about sending foreigners to Mount Igman if they refused to participate in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that, really. I really don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, again in the first six months of 1993, discussions at the 3rd Corps concerning foreign fighters, persons from Asian or African countries?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, no. I was not a participant in such a discussion, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember at any point in time, sir, discussing the issue of Asian or African foreign fighters with any of the leadership of the 3rd Corps, such as the commander, Enver Hadzihasanovic, or the chief of staff, Dzemal Merdan, in the first six months of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember attending a meeting like that; definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Whether it was a meeting or one-on-one discussions with Commander Hadzihasanovic or his deputy, Dzemal Merdan, did you ever discuss this issue of foreign fighters in the first six months of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was a brigade commander, and my command post was at least two kilometres away from the Corps Command, so I couldn't know what they were talking about on that matter. At briefings and official meetings that I took part in, and I did take part in them from time to time, the matter of foreign fighters was not discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, "my command post was at least two kilometres away from the Corps Command," can you tell us where your command post was when you were the 301st Mechanised Brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My command post was in the building of the Chamber of Commerce across the street from the printworks in the town of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, we were talking about, or I was asking you about, any discussions in the first six months of 1993 concerning foreign fighters. Did you have any discussions, or were you at any meetings, or do you recall any time when the topic of Asian or African foreign fighters were discussed in months of July and August 1993?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attend such discussions, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd ask that this document, PT01314, be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry. No, this is fine. I was a bit too early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it P01314 or is it PT?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. It's the same thing, but P01314.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: P01314 is admitted as marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit 1193, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's just clarify, Mr. Mundis. Do you want these two pages that you have referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe it's about six pages in total, Mr. President, from the first page. I think it's uploaded in e-court. It's the first page which indicates the location and the persons present, and then the two pages we've just looked at. It can either be those three pages or the entire -- I think it's -- just those three pages, the first page and then the two pages referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Three pages in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, before we -- before we leave this document, Mr. Ribo, this excerpt or this war diary, this document that you have in front of you, have you ever seen that before today?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So before your testimony in this trial or before your testimony in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura trial, no one ever showed you this document or these pages of this document before?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn to -- I would ask the usher to return that original document. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, yesterday, you were asked a number of questions and we talked a little bit about this Vlasic operation in the spring of 1995. Do you remember talking about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a few questions about that operation and that time period, the spring, early spring, March time period, in 1995. And you told us that the El Mudjahedin Detachment was not prepared or ready to take part in this Vlasic operation at that point in time; they needed additional time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Ribo, any of the specifics, the specific reasons why the El Mudjahedin Detachment needed additional time?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, other than that they were not ready, and they reported this to the officer on duty. He informed me, and I informed the corps commander, who was at Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, who the officer on duty at this time was?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember the date, or the approximate date, when you were informed by the duty officer that he had received this report from the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the month of March - I don't know the exact date - between the 20th and the 30th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, or do you know, or did you know that the El Mudjahedin Detachment had been operating in the Zavidovici area in October/November 1994?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. At the time, I was the chief of the armoured mechanised units, and I couldn't know about the participation of all the units, where they were deployed and what they were doing at all the defence lines they were holding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will take a moment for the technical problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, we had some technical problems. I'm going to ask you that question again, and if you could please repeat the answer so we have it on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, or do you know, or did you know that the El Mudjahedin Detachment had been operating in the Zavidovici area in October/November 1994?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, because I was the chief of the armoured mechanised units at the time and I didn't have to know the areas of the units' deployment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, when did you become the chief of operations and training for the 3rd Corps, the approximate date, if you don't recall the exact date?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly, toward the end of March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I take it, then, that when you received this report or this information from the duty officer concerning the El Mudjahedin Detachment, you told us that was between the 20th and 30th of March, would that have been in the first few days that you took over this position?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first couple of days after I took up that position, I think I got the decision on my appointment on the 31st of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At that point in time, sir, when you became the chief or head of the operations and training for the 3rd Corps, to what unit was the El Mudjahedin Detachment subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not subordinated to any unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It reported directly to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an independent unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But it reported directly to the 3rd Corps commander?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This unit, the El Mudjahedin Detachment, during time periods when it was directly subordinated to the 3rd Corps commander, was used as a manoeuvre unit, was it not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't really be able to call it a manoeuvre unit, since it took part in a very small number of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But those operations it did take part in, it was used in a very specialised function, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an assault unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. It was used as a spearheading unit in some of the most difficult operations undertaken by the 3rd Corps in 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it took part in assault activities. It was not related to the defence lines. It didn't have a role to play there. It took part in assault actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. The El Mudjahedin Detachment was not used as a static unit along assigned parts of defence lines, but rather was used throughout the 3rd Corps AOR in some of the most difficult assault assignments that corps undertook in 1995; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had several manoeuvre units which were also of high quality, which is why they were given those assignments. The El Mujahid Detachment took part in assault combat actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the El Mudjahedin Detachment was one of the high-quality assault units of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: One couldn't put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, you just said, "We had several manoeuvre units which were also of high quality, which is why they were given those assignments. The El Mujahid Detachment took part in assault combat actions." My question to you is: The El Mudjahedin Detachment was one of the high-quality assault units, and that's precisely why they were given the taskings they were given?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the military aspect, no, it was not of high quality, nor was it particularly a well-trained unit. That's definitely not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ribo, on the 10th and 11th of September, you told us you were at the forward command post of the 35th Division in Babylon Restaurant; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What task was the El Mudjahedin Detachment given on the 10th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the Corps Command is concerned, it did not issue a specific task to the El Mujahid Detachment. It issued a specific assignment to the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That wasn't my question, sir. My question was: What task was the El Mudjahedin Detachment given, not which unit gave the El Mudjahedin Detachment that tasking?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The El Mujahid Detachment was given its tasks by the commander of the 35th Division, Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. I understand what you're saying, Mr. Ribo. My question wasn't who gave them the task. My question is: What was the task? What did Commander Hasanagic task the El Mudjahedin Detachment to do on 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, the commander of the 35th Division set up combined forces, including the El Mujahid Detachment, the 2nd or the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalions - I can't remember now off the top of my head - and as far as I know, they, the detachment, had the task to attack along the axis of Opaljenik and Stog.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And with respect to Paljenik, the El Mudjahedin Detachment was highly successful in capturing the Paljenik feature in the early morning of 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the interpretation of the first part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With respect to the Paljenik feature, the El Mudjahedin Detachment was highly successful in capturing the Paljenik feature in the early morning hours of 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stressed that those were combined forces, including two more manoeuvre battalions, yes. The feature, Opaljenik Mount, was, indeed, successfully captured that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I keep hearing in the translation "Opaljenik Mount." We're talking about Paljenik, not Opaljenik.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we're confusing these places. There are two different topographical positions. There is Paljenik at Vlasic, and there is Opaljenik at Zavidovici in the valley of Krivaja River.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The feature that is in the immediate vicinity of the Restaurant Babylon is which feature?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Opaljenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, that feature was taken in the early morning hours of 10 September 1995 within a matter of minutes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that operation was spearheaded by the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were several units that were subordinated to it, the 2nd or the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalions and some other brigades from the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's just get clarity here. Mr. Ribo, the translation of your answer says: "Yes. There were several units that were subordinated to it ..." Now, the "it" that is there, now which has been referred to previously, is the El Mudjahedin Detachment. Are you suggesting that several units were subordinated to the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this operation, yes. That's why the commander called them "combined units," and then he said "the Detachment of El Mujahid."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the 2nd or 3rd Manoeuvre Battalions that you indicated were subordinated to the El Mudjahedin Detachment for this operation, to what superior unit did the 2nd or 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion report to?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this operation, it was the 35th Division. Under the normal circumstances, they were subordinated to the corps commander. There were five manoeuvre battalions, and all five of them were subordinated to the commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And for this operation, the 3rd Corps commander resubordinated the manoeuvre battalions, the 2nd and 3rd Manoeuvre Battalions, to the 35th Division commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And with respect to the operation concerning Paljenik, it's your testimony, sir, that the 35th Division commander then resubordinated the 2nd or 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion to the El Mudjahedin Detachment in order to carry out the assault on Paljenik?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Paljenik feature, Mr. Ribo, was that a difficult feature to take?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a peak overlooking the entire valley of the Krivaja River. The 35th Division had tried on several occasions, let's say once or twice, to capture the elevation, but failed. The peak was only liberated in the Operation Farz.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That peak, the Paljenik feature, the top of that does not have any tree cover or any other type of brush cover, does it?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the top?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the very top, I don't think; but looking at it from the foot of the peak all the way almost through to the end, there is vegetation and there are also trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, what else can you remember about the events that happened on the 10th of September, 1995, other than this action?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me for interrupting. I'm a bit lost. We were speaking of Paljenik or Opaljenik here just now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're discussing Opaljenik, in the valley of the Krivaja River, which is from Zavidovici toward Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I had understood; but in the transcript, we read all the time "Paljenik."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, let's try to see if we can completely clear this up. There's a feature on Mount Vlasic, and your testimony is that the feature on Mount Vlasic is called "Paljenik"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just so that we are very clear, that "Paljenik" is spelled P-A-L-J-E-N-I-K?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's no "O" at the beginning of the word. That's the "Paljenik" you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
