utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this Paljenik that is a feature on Mount Vlasic is how far, approximately, how far away from the Krivaja River and Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 150 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this operation that we've been talking about that was spearheaded by the El Mudjahedin Detachment with the 2nd or 3rd Manoeuvre Battalions was, according to your testimony, at the Opaljenik feature in the Krivaja Valley near Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, on the road from Zavidovici towards Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And it's, approximately, how far from the Babylon Restaurant, where you were on that day, that served as the 35th Division forward command post?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, other than this operation to seize this feature that you've told us is Opaljenik, what other operations do you recall that took place on 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for this operation and Operation Farz, as a whole, I am not aware of there having been any other operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, just for a moment, putting aside this assault on Opaljenik in the Krivaja Valley, what other part of Operation Farz do you remember taking place on the 10th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same area, toward Vozuca, from the direction of Kamenica, the operation was carried out by the 1st Manoeuvre Battalion, 375th Liberation Brigade, 7th Chivalrous Muslim Brigade, the 5th Battalion of the 303rd Brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Attacking from the north, from the direction of Kamenica, the following operations were conducted by -- or rather, the following units: 1st Manoeuvre Battalion, 375th Liberation Brigade, 7th Chivalrous Muslim Liberation Brigade, 5th Battalion of the 303rd Brigade. These were the units attacking from the west, from the direction of the Kamenica River, or rather, also the Kamenica settlement. Now, the El Mudjahedin Detachment was attacking along the axis of the attack of the 35th Division, which went upstream alongside the Krivaja River toward Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And throughout that operation on the 10th of September, 1995, involving all of these units that you've just been talking about, you were at the forward command post of the 35th Division in Babylon Restaurant?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I was there, and two more associates of mine. The assistant commander for moral guidance and a security officer were there with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this assistant commander for moral guidance you've just mentioned is Halim Husic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halim Husic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Halim Husic was with you at that forward command post also from the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And your job there was basically to monitor progress concerning Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so, and to assist the subordinate commands where necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, do you remember, shortly after these events on 10 September 1995, speaking to a journalist by the name of Adnon Dzonlic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember speaking to him. This journalist was a member of the Information Service of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And his job was to write articles for newsletters and magazines of the 3rd Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military magazines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which were, in part, to serve as a historical record, but also to build morale of the soldiers in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the magazines were primarily published to provide information to the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And one of those publications is called "Prva Linija"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it wasn't a publication of the 3rd Corps. It is, indeed, a military publication, but not of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which military unit is responsible for Prva Linija?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember if it was the General Staff or the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown the document P02696, P02696.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, do you see on the screen in front of you a copy of "Prva Linija"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you see, sir, where, to the left-hand side under the word "Linija," it says: "List Armija RBiH"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ribo, that would indicate that this is a magazine or a publication of the Army of the RBiH?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this copy of the magazine or journal is dated 1 October 1995. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask if we could please go to the page bearing ERN number 0469-6976, 0469-6976. And in English, this is page 9, I believe. Let's start on page 6, actually, in the English, please, and it's the bottom half of page 6 in English, the bottom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, do you see this article: "The 'Chetnik Stalingrad' Liberated," by Adnan Dzonlic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see that, but I can't make out the rest. It's quite poor, the copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this before, sir? Do you remember seeing this perhaps when it was published?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it at some point, but I can't remember when that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. This is the journalist that you spoke to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did speak with him, but very briefly. Later, I can clarify how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let's just start, if we could, if we could go, please, to the right-hand column in the middle of the page in Bosnian, and page 9 in the English translation, and about the middle of the page in the English version on page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, reference to -- or your name as a source for this story?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And it says: "We have learned about the final assault on the Chetnik front lines around Vozuca in the conversation with Colonel Hasim Riba"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ribo, you were a source, were you not, for the information that's contained in this article?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly, but not in the verbal sense. A few sentences, I did say; but for the rest, I gave him the document. I gave him the entire order for the assault operation, and he copied from that. I didn't have time to speak with him for long and to give him all the specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, do you confirm that "Colonel Hasim Riba" written in this document refers to Haso Ribo, yourself? You confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ribo, a few moments ago, you told us that you could explain how this article was written, and I think you've just done that. In effect, you spoke briefly to Mr. Dzonlic, and then you provided him with the document or documents relating to this operation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, because these are documents from the initial phase of the operation; and because he was a member of the 3rd Corps Command Information Service, I told him, "Here's the order. So you can write on the basis of the order, this is the practical action of the units in this action. So that is what you can do." So he did copy from the order, and you can see, from the map, that it is actually a copy of the orders that I actually issued to the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, of course, when you spoke to him, since this article is in a magazine dated 1 October 1995, I assume, sir, that you spoke to him almost immediately after this operation had been undertaken.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date when I spoke with him. I really cannot remember, but I was with him very briefly. This initial part, if you looked at the map yesterday that I was explaining, this is the initial phase of the operation, and he's describing the initial phase of the operation here, the entry into Vozuca, but not the further course of the operation on Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But it would have been obviously sometime after the 10th of September, 1995 and before the 1st of October, 1995, when you spoke to this journalist?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in that period from September 10th until the end of October. Probably, this is the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd ask that P02696 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object to the admission of this whole document into evidence since this document actually contains two articles, one that begins on page ending with numbers 6974, and the witness didn't even see that. He didn't have the opportunity to look at it. The other is the article that has been shown to the witness now, which begins on page 046969, and ends with the page -- ends on this page 96976. So I object to material being admitted that the witness hadn't even seen, and never mind commented upon. Otherwise, this is also an exhibit with a large number of pages, as far as I can see, and it contains a number of different articles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fair enough, Your Honours. We're simply tendering those pages which are this very article. We'd ask that the cover page be admitted and the three-page article that the witness has testified about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, excuse me. It has escaped me what the significance of this article is, other than the fact that the witness spoke to the journalist, who then wrote the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it would be our submission that it's a contemporaneous account of what happened in an official army publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But rather than asking the Judges then to read the article, I think it would be more prudent to elicit this information directly from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm happy to do that, if you would prefer me to do that. I'm basically going to read the article to him and put questions, if you'd prefer me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If that's the way you want to proceed, I just thought that you were going to put the article away now, without having --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I can certainly do that. We can go paragraph by paragraph and I can put questions to him, or we could simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- put the article in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please don't. Proceed the way you had thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would just tender the cover page and the three pages that constitute this article, which are the ERN numbers -- the three-page article being 0469-6976 through 0469-6978, and the cover page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, let me just be clear that, Judge Harhoff, are you withdrawing, sir, what you were asking Mr. Mundis to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes and no. What I want to know, when we are finished with this article, is what the information is relating to the actions of the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. I still don't understand now, when you say "Yes and no," Judge, because Mr. Mundis said, "I can certainly do that. We can go paragraph by paragraph, and I can put questions to him," and you said, "Please don't."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. President, I withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Judge. Mr. Mundis, you say we admit pages 0469 to 6976 -- I beg your pardon, 0469-6976 through to 0469-6978?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Plus the cover page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Plus the cover page. Well, the cover page of this magazine, together with pages 0469-6976 through to 0469-6978, are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the following pages will become Exhibit 1194.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, what was 1193, ma'am? Yes, I know now what it was. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, are you familiar with a journal or a magazine called "The Patriotic List"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What can you tell us about that publication?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure. Perhaps it's a wartime periodical of the 3rd Corps to keep the members of the 3rd Corps informed. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown P02747. If we could go to the page bearing ERN number 0093-0229 in the Bosnia, and I'll give you the ERN number for the English, which is 0093-1503.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, have you seen this article before?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please go to the page in Bosnian bearing ERN number 0233, and in English bearing ERN number 1515.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, at the bottom of this, that this article is also written by Mr. Adnan Dzonlic?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we now go, in the Bosnian version, to the page bearing ERN number 0232, and the English version bearing ERN number 1507. Now, if we could zoom in to the middle of the page in the Bosnian version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, to the left of the photograph, there is a paragraph that refers to Colonel Ribo?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In English, it's towards the bottom. It's now being scrolled up. It's the paragraph that begins: "We learned about the final strike ..." Is that reference, sir, to you as again being the source for Adnan Dzonlic in preparing this article?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From what I was able to notice earlier, it's the same article as the same one earlier in the patriotic paper, and it has the same order. It seems to me that it's almost an -- the identical text, because the editor of this paper, Patriotski List, issued by the 3rd Corps, was Spahija Kozlic, and his officer for information is this Adnan Dzonlic. So he's the author of both articles, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's clear, sir, Adnan Dzonlic is the article of -- is the author of both of these articles, but I would suggest to you that there are some slight differences between the two articles.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I didn't read the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could please, in the Bosnian version, zoom back out a little bit and go to the top part of the middle column. The English version is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please take a look at this part that's now visible, sir, on the screen. Sir, can you tell us, were you the source of that information, or do you know what the source of that information is?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we need to go back a little bit to the beginning, so I can see what this is about. I think the units are listed, but I don't see the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we zoom out on that, perhaps go to the bottom of the preceding column.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is all right. I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And for this part, we need to go to page 1059 in the English, and we're in the bottom half of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, do you recall being the source of the information contained in this part of the article?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that same procedure was valid. I gave the combat documents for the journalist to copy the engagement of the units. It was a written document. I don't know what the journalist actually wrote. I didn't have the opportunity to actually read this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me go to one more part of this article. In Bosnian, it's page 0231; and in the English, it's 1507. And in the Bosnian, it's the far-right column under the photo. And in the English, we need to just go up a little bit to capture that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, can you take a look at this part written at the top of the Bosnian language version of this article.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment, sir, or do you know anything about the reference here to taking a number of Chetnik officers prisoners, in relation to this operation at Paljenik?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know about the officers captured at a later stage who were brought to the forward command post at Natron in Maglaj, but I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it then, sir, that with respect to these captured Chetnik prisoners, as reported in this 3rd Corps magazine, "Patriotic List," you were not the source of that information.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have here begins the sentence about the actual -- "We learned about the final strike on Chetnik lines around Vozuca from Colonel Ribo, Haso," this is where my text actually begins.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You also told us you provided journalist, Adnan Dzonlic, with some documents or a document. Do you recall if the written material you gave him made reference to Chetnik officers being captured by the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, definitely not. I gave the journalist in question the combat document that was entitled, "Order for Battle," where the use of the units was precisely regulated, then he copied that, and then he used it according to his methods as a writer, a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say, sir, "his methods as a writer, as a journalist," do you know if Mr. Dzonlic's methods would have included both speaking to officers and also referring to or looking at or being provided with official documents?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would ask that P02747 be admitted, and I will specify again the page numbers just as they relate to this article. In Bosnian, it's 0093-0229 through 0093-0233, and the corresponding English translation runs from ERN range 0093-1503 through 0093-1515.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Sorry. I guess I don't need to repeat those pages. They are quite clear from the record. They're admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will become Exhibit number 1195, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, yesterday, there was a lengthy bit of your testimony that had to do with a tank. Do you remember that part of the discussion?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And there were some questions about a document that seemed to say that the tank was given to the 3rd Tank Company of the 3rd Corps, and you told us that that was incorrect, that the El Mudjahedin Detachment kept that tank. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I believe you also told us - and this is reflected on pages 7036 and 7037 - that the tank wasn't given to the 3rd Tank Company, but rather the 3rd Tank Company manned the tank, but the tank remained with the El Mudjahedin Detachment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The 3rd Tank Company provided a crew to service the tank because the El Mujahid Detachment did not permit the tank to leave their zone. It was in their zone, the zone of the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I take it, Mr. Ribo, that the El Mudjahedin Detachment did not have personnel who were qualified, or competent, for that matter, to operate a tank.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it didn't. From what I knew, if they did have that, they wouldn't request people from the 3rd Tank Company to operate the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I believe this was a T-55 tank. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, if this was the only T-55 tank that the El Mudjahedin Detachment captured in 1995, or were there other tanks?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall, but I believe that it was only this tank. According to my information, it was only this tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And just as the El Mudjahedin Detachment didn't have personnel who were qualified to operate the tank, they also lacked experienced personnel who could service and maintain this tank; wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct. They didn't have any specially-trained personnel in order to be able to maintain and service that type of combat vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You're a former armoured officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I'm sure you'd agree with me that servicing and maintaining a T-55 tank, so that it's actually operational, is not something that the average person on the street can do?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, when this T-55 tank that the El Mudjahedin Detachment captured required servicing or maintenance, they would require the support and assistance of the 3rd Corps 3rd Tank Company; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct that it was the 3rd Tank Company; but as part of the 3rd Corps Logistics, there was a section for the maintenance of tanks in all units, in the 3rd Tank Company and also in the 37th Tank Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me see if I can clear this up, and I think it will be an appropriate time for the break. Let me just see if I understand this. The 3rd Tank Company provided the crew to operate the tank while it was with the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But it was the 3rd Corps Logistics Service that provided maintenance and servicing for the tank, just like they did for the 3rd Tank Company and the 37th Tank Company of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I also assume, Mr. Ribo, that you don't buy ordnance for a T-55 tank on the streets in Zavidovici or Zenica.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, you don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So the 3rd Corps Logistics Department was also providing any ordnance, ammunition, et cetera, that this T-55 tank required in order to be fully operational?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They captured the tank, and it was full of ammunition. They did have ammunition in the tank. It was completely fully stocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That would seem to be quite a coup. Do you know if, during the course of 1995, that tank required additional ammunition or ordnance?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be an appropriate time for the break. I have just a couple of issues. I won't be much longer after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I just have a few more questions for you concerning just a couple of topics. The first one -- the first topic I want to go back to is this issue of the logbooks or war diaries and how they were paginated and certified. And I know you spoke about that over the last couple of days. Let's just start with this process of paginating the books, paginating the diaries or the logs. Let me see if I understand correctly how that works. When you paginate the books, you do that before the logbooks are actually filled in; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Before any entry is made in the diary, that has to be dealt with. The pages have to be paginated, the appropriate writing must be made at the end, then it must be also registered with a logbook, and only then can you start writing entry into the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you get a blank notebook or logbook, it's completely blank, Then you hand-number each of the pages from 1 to 95, however many pages are in the book; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, because it's governed by the rules of handling office material, and we had to abide by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And then after you've hand-paginated the book, at the end of the book, on the last page, the back of the last page, you write a declaration as to how many pages the book has, you signed it, and you put a stamp on it?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the last page of the notebook, you have to write down that this notebook has such-and-such a number of pages. Then I have to place my name, my rank and position, I have to sign it, and only then is it entered into the logbook of operational notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And then someone else, perhaps from the Operations Centre, puts the actual lines with the column headings and fills in all of the template, if you will, for the logbook; someone else does that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And then the individual duty officers actually make the various entries and sign at the end of their shifts?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the notebook in question, on the type of data entered, and so on and so forth. For instance, the book of duty officers has such a procedure that, in the left column, you have the signature of the person taking over from the person who was there previously, who will place his signature on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And all of this is done pursuant to some kind of instruction or regulation?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I take it, sir, from that answer, that you're not in a position to tell us why it was done that way. You simply did it that way; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's regulated in --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness answered that it was done in accordance with the office procedure, the office rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that was not the question, Madam Vidovic. The question was, "You don't know why the procedure was like that; you just did it like that?" I'm not quite sure you're on the page with your colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps I might just rephrase to see if we can get the same information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I asked this question because it seems a bit strange that you would certify how many pages the book has before all of the pages have been filled out and completed.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was done in accordance with the rules on office procedure. Not a single piece of data could be entered into the book before the book has been paginated, certified at the end, and entered into the logbook of operational notebooks. These were the rules, and one could not depart from them, not for any particular notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I understand what you're saying, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now, with the assistance of the usher, that the witness be shown P511 [sic], the original which I have here in my hand, and I would ask that that be placed on the ELMO so that we can all take another look at this. For the record, this is Exhibit 511, not P511. This is Exhibit 511. This is the original. Now, if we could please turn to page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ribo, we see now before us page 15 of Exhibit 511, and that seems to be filled out -- that page seems to be filled out completely, right to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could maybe see the whole page, please, and if we could zoom out and see the whole page. Yeah, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if you need to, Mr. Ribo, the original is actually on the machine next to you. It might be easier for you to look at. I don't know. You see page 15 is filled out completely, right to the bottom of the page; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn to page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I note, sir, that you only paginate the front side of each page, is that correct, so that there are no numbers on the left-hand side at the top of the document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you understand me correctly. We paginated the pages of the notebook. This was page number 15, the one we looked at -- or rather, the sheet, and then it has its front and back page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you only put the number on the front side of each page?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We placed the number on the sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Right, okay. So each page -- so page 15 has a front side and a back side?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sheet number 15 has the front and back cover. Had the clause indicated that the book had 56 pages, then they would all have been numbered, the front and the back pages would be numbered; whereas, the -- those that are numbered are merely sheets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So if we could please then see the right-hand side of this, so we can see page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, Mr. Ribo, page 16 is completely filled out to the bottom of that page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Turn that page over, and we'll see the back of page 16 is also completely filled out to the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next page, which is blank, contains the number "17"?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But there were no entries made on page 17?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not even the columns were drawn. I don't know why. One did not have to draw the columns before filling the book. What mattered were the numbers at the top. That's what mattered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Exactly. I'm not disagreeing with you at all, sir. And, quite often, I would imagine that the duty officer, when he came in to take over his shift, probably put those lines in, because there might not be a lot going on at 1.00 in the morning and he has plenty of time to actually draw the lines and the columns on those pages. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fully. The officer had time enough to draw the columns and make the entries. That's only logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let's go to the next page, then, if we can see that and down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Page 18, again nothing written on the page. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, and that would appear to be page 19; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sheet number 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sheet 19. And the next page, what page is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sheet 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are you sure it's 21? I think it might be 91.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And we can actually see, on the ELMO, in between the pages, where a number of pages have been removed from this diary; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But I suggest to you, Mr. Ribo, if we go back to page 17, for whatever reason, this diary ends at the entry on the bottom of the back side of page 16.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what we can see here, that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Right. Because they wouldn't or they shouldn't have left pages 17, 18, and 19 blank, and then resumed on page 21 or 22 of the diary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be normal for them to take it sheet by sheet. Now, why somebody should come up with the idea of skipping a couple of pages, I don't know. It would be only normal to take it sheet by sheet; although, it wouldn't be a disaster if they skipped one page. They could cross it out, they could even skip it, they could do whatever they wanted with it, except for tearing it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Right. I agree there is something that is abnormal about a number of pages being taken out, but I suggest to you, because pages 17, 18, and 19 remain in the book and are blank, that this war diary ends at the bottom of the back side of page 16.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim that because I don't know when the notebook started, with what date, and when it ended, so I can't really state that with any certainty. I can only observe that several sheets are missing. That's definitely the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But the sheets before the missing sheets are in the book, they're paginated, and they're blank?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that. I've just observed that the diary was kept until the 9th of October, so that, really, I doubt the authenticity of this document. I don't know. I have my doubts as to why there are no more entries made in this diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But what I'm saying to you, sir, is that the following pages, the following three or four pages, are properly paginated and they're blank, and there's really no dispute about that whatsoever, is there?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if you go to the page immediately after that part where the pages have been removed, the pages resume at page 91, continue to the end of the book, and are also blank?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. That exhibit can be removed. We're done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. Witness, to your knowledge, according to the practice you were following, since you told us that those pages were written upon and certification was done before the book was being used -- the book was used, have there been other cases where only part of the book was used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of such cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to you, the book should have been used until the last page, until the end, where there was a certification of the number of pages, according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Lattanzi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me pick up on that, then, Mr. Ribo, because again you've told us earlier that you certify the book before there's any entries made in the book.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If I could retrieve Exhibit 511, and I'd now like to show the witness Exhibit 394.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, I would ask you to go to page 15 of this diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we could then flip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We see that page 15 is completely filled out to the bottom of the page; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Where is page 15? Where is the number "15"? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You see page 15 is filled out to the bottom of the page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And page 16 stops towards the top of the page; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page. Page 17 is blank?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Page 18 is blank?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Page 19 is blank?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Page 20, there were some papers inserted into that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 20 is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can we see the upper right-hand corner of this page. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So we, again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is that figure? Is that "42"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because the witness said page 20 is missing. Is it page 20 up to page 41 that are missing, or is it just page 20 that is missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sheet number 20 is missing, and all the other sheets up to 42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, if we go back, though, sir, to page 16, we clearly have another logbook that is not filled in all the way to the end of the book; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the same diary. It's not another diary. It's simply the case of the columns not having been filled out fully on page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, it would seem that this diary stops with the entry on the top of the page 16.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I can see, that's the case. The entries were made up until sheet 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, in fact, this book wasn't completed or wasn't filled out until the very last page in the book?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It hasn't been completed either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when these books are completed or when they've -- when they're full or when they're no longer used, are they again in any way certified by anyone?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are handed over to the office and are signed off in the logbook in which they were entered as issued, and sent to the files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But are they certified by anyone? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nobody certifies that. Only the person who keeps records, the logbooks of the book having been issued, takes it in and puts it on the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ribo, that's why I asked you a question right after the break about a policy or a regulation or instruction that requires you to certify the number of pages in a blank document before all those pages are filled in. That's a bit of an odd way of certifying these books. I understand it's the instruction, but it's a bit of an odd way of doing things, that you would certify how many pages are in it before anything's written in it.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This wasn't only the case in the army. It was also the case in the former Yugoslav People's Army, in the Territorial Defence. Practically, as far as I know, there were some minor modifications made, but that was practically it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And these diaries or logs, such as the one you have in front of you, Exhibit 394, or the one we just looked at, Exhibit 511, which section or department within the 3rd Corps was responsible for maintaining these documents?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the Department for Operations and Training and the duty officer at the Corps Command and at the IKM, forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So it was actually the department that you headed that was responsible for maintaining these documents?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That exhibit can be removed from the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I just have really one last topic, just a couple of questions. Mr. Ribo, yesterday, there were some comments made about documents that you had been involved in drafting that had some inaccurate information. And on page 7046 of yesterday's hearing, at lines 10 to 12, you were asked by my learned colleague from the Defence: "Mr. Ribo, did you write inaccurate documents during the war?" And the answer was: "No. A mistake, small, minor mistake could slip by, but no." Do you remember that question and your answer?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: These minor mistakes, mistake, or mistakes that you mentioned, the ones that you say could slip by, did you notice these mistakes at the time you drafted the documents or only when you came here to court and were shown the documents?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, I'd observe them at the point when I'd be sending them out, and I'd realise that they didn't really have the proper military form, they have errors. Sometimes, I'd notice these errors only once the documents were shown to me here. With hindsight and the experience I have now, I'd never repeat the same mistakes again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. When you observe them, when you send them out, you send them out to where, sir? Your answer was: "Sometimes, I would observe them at the point when I'd be sending them out ..." Sending them out where to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I made the draft version of the document in my handwriting, then I give the document to be typewritten, and then ultimately the document is sent to the addressee. Then once the document has been sent out, it comes back to the person who has drafted it to be filed or to simply have it there to see what the follow-up requested in the document has been.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With respect, sir, to the answer, when you said, at line 11 and 12 of page 35, "Sometimes I'd observe them at the point when I'd be sending them out," when you found mistakes at that point in time, sir, why didn't you take steps to correct the document, if you spotted, as you were sending it out, that it had inaccurate information?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it more applied to when the document was returned to me to be archived. Then I would look and see that I perhaps made a mistake or slipped in a small way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ribo. The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few questions only, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good day again, Mr. Ribo. In response to questions by the Prosecutor, you talked about a meeting with the commander of the Patriotic League in the situation when he received 40.000 marks from a foreign donor. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that his name was Mr. Puric and that he invited you, if I understood correctly, to witness that act.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is true, to witness that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, was Mr. Puric a subordinate of yours or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when this happened, were you there to be a witness when he received the money in his capacity as commander or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at MFI 1193.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, while we are waiting for the document, I'm just going to remind you that this is something that the Prosecutor described or called a diary that describes some meeting in the village of Biljesevo. What I'd like to ask you is this: It has to do with the record books that you testified about a little bit earlier, please. All the books of records, including working notebooks, according to the rules on office procedure in the former SFRY and in Bosnia-Herzegovina during the war, had to be paginated and certified?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document here that you saw, that the Prosecutor showed you the original, were the sheets numbered, and was the book or the notebook or the diary, however you want to describe it, was that certified?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not marked. The sheets or the pages were not numbered. It was not certified at the back, and it was not entered in the protocol of books or notebooks issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And such a document, was it considered to be an official document or not?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our military rules, it was not considered that. In the courts of former Yugoslavia, especially the military courts recognised only information from the work books that were certified and entered into the protocol books, as being books issued within a unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Maybe we can put this protocol away. Can we look at Exhibit 1195 briefly. Can we look at page 0093-0232, the page ending with the numbers 0232, 0232. I'm talking about an exhibit. Can we please look at the middle column so that the witness can see what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also showed you this part that described the direction of movement of the El Mudjahedin Detachment in this article, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, are we having the equivalent of this middle column on the English side?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the page we see does not correspond to the B/C/S. The corresponding page is the one that ends with 1509, 1509. I apologise, I didn't notice this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, here, in this part of the text, you can see the journalist's description of the movement of the El Mudjahedin Detachment during the Farz action. Please, did you describe to Journalist Adnan Dzonlic the movement of the El Mudjahedin Detachment? Are you the source of that information during this Farz action?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is his own phrasing. I gave him a document for all units, a document entitled, "Order," "Zapovjest," and he copied that document on his own.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. When we talk about what you gave him, you said that you gave him an order determining the axes of attack. I would like to ask you - let's be as specific as possible - was this an order of the 3rd Corps or of some other unit? What did you give him? What kind of an order was it?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an order of the Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you this: Did an order of the 3rd Corps contain information about the movement of the El Mudjahedin Detachment, this order that you gave, "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection. Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's leading, and I'll reiterate what I've said the past two days concerning the overlap between my learned colleague and the witness, and leading questions on both direct examination and re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I put the question. I'm just reading it in the transcript. I'm sorry for rushing perhaps to gain time. I put the question, "if that order contained the axis or not," so I don't know how that would be suggestive. Perhaps it is a little bit clear. I see that now on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I asked: "Did or did it not, this order, include the axes of movement of the El Mudjahedin Detachment?"

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps order for the Operation Farz at Vozuca did not contain the tasks, meaning we did not issue -- the Command of the 3rd Corps did not issue a task to the El Mujahid Detachment, but it issued an assignment to the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now let me ask you this: So this document that you gave, or documents in general that you gave, could have served as the basis of this story by the journalist?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that possibly the journalist used documents of the 35th Division in writing this article.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, but I'm asking you specifically. The document that you -- or documents that you gave to the journalist, could they or it have served as the basis or as the source of this story about the movement of the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It did not, or they did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: These are leading questions, and that question, the last question, is the same question that the witness had just answered previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may respond. When I objected to questions by the Prosecutor, I didn't say, "This is a leading question." The Prosecutor should say, "In what way this constitutes a leading question. This is an open-ended question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think the question suggested the answer, and that is the definition of a leading question. When the question is phrased in such a way as, "Could it have served as the basis or source of this story," that suggests that the answer is either "yes" or "no," which is a textbook example of a leading question, rather than, "What were the sources of the journalist's story," or, "What information did the journalist base the story on," or, "What documents did the journalist base the story on," rather than, "Could this document" or "Could that document be the basis or the source for the story?"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not share the Prosecutor's opinion. I don't see in which way -- well, the question is very important. So I don't see in what way could I put it other than, "Did this that you gave serve as the basis for the journalist's story?" In any case, the witness answered and it's in the transcript, and I just briefly wish to put only two questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Court please rule on the objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled. You may proceed, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What for? You have no reason to apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, for not stopping in time so that you could resolve this objection. This is my apology.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday I put this question to you, and today the Prosecutor put specific questions to you, about the tank. It was Exhibit 1188. You explained that on the basis of this document -- you remember that document? I don't have to show it to you, do I? You remember it?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, you said that the El Mudjahedin Detachment captured that document. That tank, was there an order or a request of the corps -- any kind of request from the corps regarding that tank?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an order from the Corps Command that the tank should be handed over to the 3rd Tank Company because it was a unit that was intended -- it was an armoured mechanised unit in the 3rd Corps that had all the tanks in the 3rd Corps, and that was that 3rd Tank Company and the 37th Tank Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Please, so you explained to us - you don't have to repeat it - that the tank did not go to this unit, but that it -- the crew from that unit went off to operate that tank; do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, did the El Mudjahedin Detachment ultimately respect the order of the corps or not, in view of that tank, or it did something that they felt was fit or appropriate?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: A leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase it, Your Honours, if you allow me. I accept. I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was, indeed, a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll rephrase it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, ultimately, what happened regarding this tank, in terms of the order from the corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The El Mujahid Detachment did not obey the order for the tank to be handed over to the 3rd Company, and the Corps Command informed the chief of the armoured mechanised units at the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, I'm going to put just one more question to you about this last document, the war diary, the last document that we looked at. This is Exhibit 394. You leafed through it. You noticed that the document was numbered up to page 19 or 20, and then what follows is page 41. According to customary practice, is something like that possible or not, when we look at documents?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you talked about a military unit. Was this a military unit right from the start or was it a political entity first of all? I'm talking about the Patriotic Unit.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know the way and the system in which the Patriotic League functioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you don't know whether right from the start it was a military unit or not that was going to battle against the enemy of Bosnia-Herzegovina or whether, instead, it was an association, an organisation, or a political party that recruited volunteers to fight the enemy?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, this was not a political organisation. It was some form of military organising, not entirely so, but they were working to prepare the population for the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They were a clandestine organisation in the beginning. Nobody knew about them. It was a clandestine organisation, but later they declared themselves openly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it wasn't composed of military personnel, professional military personnel or reservists?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They didn't even have uniforms. They simply operated in civilian clothes in certain municipalities, sectors, in villages, but they were not uniformed persons. They were not allowed to wear uniforms. I think they were founded before the beginning of the armed conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but I don't know any details about them, not really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I right to understand that afterwards, when the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was set up, that they were integrated, incorporated into the army; or, rather, the individuals that were members of the Patriotic League integrated a unit or entered a unit of the army? I'm afraid I don't remember which one.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, individuals, yes, they joined the brigades that were in their area, but most of them went into politics. It was much easier to be a politician than a soldier at that period. Among others, we have the example of Zihnija Aganovic, who was originally the commander of the Regional Staff of the Patriotic League, only to become the president of the Travnik District later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. One last question, once again, about the article drafted by this journalist. You said to us that you provided him with information, verbally - that is what I understood and you should correct me if I'm mistaken - and that you also gave him a written order, the written order of the 3rd Corps to the 35th Division, with the tasks to be accomplished; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke to him very briefly; and as I stated when I was looking at the article, I only spoke to him by way of an introduction briefly. I then gave him documents which he then freely interpreted in his article that was ultimately published in "Patriotski List" and this other publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we, once again, take a look at this article, the last article we had up on the screen, the journalist's article. Let me ask you just one thing. Given that you spoke to us about many things concerning the El Mudjahedin Detachment during the Farz Operation, in particular as regards the questions raised by Mrs. Vidovic on the tank, is it possible -- Next page, please. Could we see the next page on the screen. Next page in the English version, please. Is it possible that where a reference is made halfway through the page, after Mala Satnica: [In English] "The task was completed. It united the units under the commander ..." [Interpretation] Is it possible that these details concerning the El Mudjahedin Detachment and the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion - I'm afraid I'm not very well acquainted with the military terminology - the 4th Battalion, the 5th Battalion, that all these details could have been inferred from the order that the 3rd Corps was giving to the 35th Division or perhaps from the conversation, the direct conversation that you had with the journalist? Because as regards the examination, the cross-examination, and the additional questions, there were doubts about the source. That's why I want to elucidate this aspect.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that the journalist -- or rather, I presume that the journalist took the information from the Command of the 35th Division, because that's not the way the corps formulated it. We wrote the task for the 35th Division. We didn't go into the lower-level subordinated units. It was the commander of the 35th Division who issued the order, in turn, to his subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. But since you seem to be familiar with many things concerning this operation, in particular, relating to the El Mudjahedin Detachment, perhaps some of the details came out of your direct conversation with the journalist, or do you exclude that completely, categorically?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever was under the command of the 3rd Corps, directly under the command of the 3rd Corps, I could explain to him directly because I knew about that. Whatever had to do with the 35th Division or the 7th Muslim Brigade, that sort of information he could have gotten out in the field from the commander of the 35th Division or the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. It could have come from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May I just have a few questions to the witness. The first question relates to the perception that you had about the El Mudjahedin Detachment. When I asked you about this yesterday or the day before, you seemed to acknowledge that, yes, on the one hand, the El Mujahid Detachment was known as a brave and courageous unit; yet, on the other hand, they were also -- I think I used the word "lazy," and you used another word, but the gist of your answer to me was that they were difficult to cooperate with because they only took part in the action when they wanted. Today, you informed us further on this issue, and you said that they were neither a very effective unit, nor were they very well trained, and I want your evaluation of the El Mujahid Detachment as a partner in the conflict. Can you -- in your capacity as chief of operations of the 3rd Corps, you must have had a pretty good view or grasp of the way in which the different units functioned, and we have also received information that the El Mujahid Detachment was an assault unit, along with two or three other similar assault units. Now, could you give us your evaluation, in terms of a comparison between the El Mujahid Detachment and the two or three other assault units under the authority of the 3rd Corps? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can tell you that we, in the 3rd Corps, had far better units than the El Mujahid Detachment. If we look at Operation Farz only and we look at the western flank and the units attacking from there, and the terrain that they had to cross over, such as the 1st Manoeuvre Battalion, such as the 7th Muslim Liberation Brigade, the 375th Brigade, we had far better units than the El Mujahid Detachment ever was. These units were very successful; and on the 10th of September, in Operation Farz, they managed to accomplish their tasks under very difficult conditions. In my view, as a soldier, they were able to overcome far more difficult tasks than El Mujahid ever could. I don't think that by any standards could the El Mujahid Detachment be ranked higher than the units that belonged to the establishment. I can tell you, sitting here, that we had units that were far better than the El Mujahid Detachment. These units could take our orders whenever and head out into battle, be it within the AOR of the 3rd Corps or of any other corps. This, however, was not the case with the El Mujahid Detachment. They were encamped and they needed considerable time to get ready and to get engaged in whatever combat assignments their superior gave them or would give them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And give me, if you can, a brief answer. By what standards or what criteria do you make this comparison?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: By their performance in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yet we have seen today and we have had other information during this trial that the success of the El Mujahid Detachment was quite impressive, in particular in relation to the seizure of the Paljenik feature or the, as you call it, Opaljenik feature.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we looked at the map of Operation Farz and if we looked at the other units that took part in the assault actions, we would be able to gauge the area which the El Mudjahedin Detachment attacked. They had only one elevation point and only the village of Stog that they were attacking, and that's where their mission was over, whereas the other units had to break the enemy lines, and when they reached Vozuca, we ordered them to continue chasing the enemy. That was the tactical order. We wanted to be at the heels of the enemy so that they cannot defend themselves. This was not the case with the El Mujahid. The El Mujahid unit merely took -- captured Opaljenik and the village of Stog, together with the other units with whom they had to coordinate their activities, and that was the end of the story for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me move on because the time is short. Let me move on to the tank issue which we have spoken a lot about today. If I have understood this correctly, the tank was seized by the El Mujahid Detachment and was kept under or was kept within their camp or their control, yet we've also heard that the tank was, in fact, operated by the 3rd Corps. And this doesn't make sense to me, because if the tank was actually used later on in combat and it was operated by units of the 3rd Corps, then why didn't the drivers of the tank just drive away with the tank after the operation? This is maybe a very naive question. But once you have the drivers and the team inside the tank, and it is operating, it's firing, and then at a certain point the battle stops, the natural thing would be then just to drive home to the 3rd Corps with the thing?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand what you're saying, but that would mean that you would lose your head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: How so?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, very well so. They'd find you. They'd search you out, find you, and kill you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You mean afterwards. Even so, if the driver of the 3rd Corps would drive the tank back to the 3rd Corps --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes,.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- then the El Mujahed soldiers would know who it was who drove the tank and then come after them afterwards?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ribo, the war diaries that you were using or that we saw here today, did they all come from the unit that was under you, the department?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The war diaries and all the notebooks that are kept, I was the one to open the documents and get them ready for use. That's precisely the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You did that for the entire units of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I did that only for the purposes of the Command of the 3rd Corps. Whatever the 3rd Corps Command used was within my competence. All the subordinate commands had their protocols, their books and people in charge of them. I worked solely for the 3rd Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The war diaries or the documents, the diaries that you were shown here today, I think you were shown three, do they all come from the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But were they issued by you? That's what I want to know.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two documents that are up there, I was the one who numbered them, signed them, and issued them for use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm asking you about all the war diaries that you have been shown in this court. Were they all issued by you?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't issue one of them, the one relating to -- perhaps I could indicate the one that I did not issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can do so, with the help of the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had never seen this document or taken any part in issuing it. I don't know who issued the document or anything like that. As for the others, I issued them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please specify the number of the document the witness is referring to? Let us know that this is MFI 1193, because the witness has been referring to it as "this document," and later on we won't know which one it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Do we confirm that it is MFI 1193?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Does MFI 1193 purport to be a 3rd Corps document?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't state that with any certainty. It doesn't have a stamp. I don't know if it's a document of the 3rd Corps. I was probably away from the 3rd Corps Command at the time, and I can't make any such statement about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When were you away from the 3rd Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was away from the 3rd Corps Command at the time when I was the commander of the 301st Mechanised Brigade, between the 28th of November, 1992 and the 30th of November, 2003 [as interpreted]. In that period, I was not a member of the 3rd Corps Command. I was the commander of the 301st Mechanised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1993 or 2003? The date in transcript, I'm not sure I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "2003", I was going to ask that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was the command of the 301st Mechanised Brigade between the 28th of November, 1992 and the 30th of November, roughly 30, the end of November, 1993. In that period of time, I was not a member of the 3rd Corps Command, I was a brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much. I can't pursue my questions. Any questions arising from the questions by the Trial Chamber, starting with you, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I just have one question arising from Judge Harhoff's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ribo, earlier today, in response to some questions I asked you, the picture that was portrayed was that the El Mudjahedin Detachment was spearheading operations; and in response to questions put to you by Judge Harhoff, you seem to portray the El Mudjahedin Detachment as being ineffective. My question to you, sir, in light of these two positions that you've told us about that seem to be contradictory, is the following: If the Mujahedin Detachment was being used to spearhead operations and that unit was ineffective, from a military point of view, would it be fair to say that the 3rd Corps or the 35th Division was using that unit on suicide missions?

utterances.speaker: HASO RIBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question. I was asked about the efficiency of the unit, and I was asked to compare this unit with the other ones of the 3rd Corps. I said that the El Mujahid Detachment was by no standards a unit better than our other units, such as the manoeuvre battalions, the liberation brigades, and so on and so forth. Here, the 35th Division commander ordered the El Mujahid Detachment to get engaged, together with the 2nd and 3rd Manoeuvre Battalions. These were combined forces, and all these forces were, in practical terms, assault units. However, here the El Mujahid Detachment was given the role of combining these two or three or how many there were units of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But, sir, if the - and I am aware of the time, Your Honours - if the El Mudjahedin Detachment was ineffective and the 2nd and 3rd Manoeuvre Battalions were highly effective units, why did the 35th Division commander subordinate those manoeuvre battalions to the El Mudjahedin Detachment rather than vice versa?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness is called to speculate. How could he know anything about what the 35th Division commander was doing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The witness very well may have a basis for answering that question, or it goes to the issue that I put in the previous question to the witness, that perhaps the El Mudjahedin Detachment was being used to undertake, in effect, suicide missions, was being sent places, because if they were ineffective and yet spearheading operations, there has to be some explanation for why they were being used in that role.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe if you just stay with that question, rather than the second one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't claim that they were completely inefficient. You asked me the question which said that they were one of the most elite units of the 3rd Corps, and this is out of the question. We had far better units, such as the 7th Muslim. We had five manoeuvre battalions which were 100 per cent better than the El Mujahid Detachment. In this situation, they were given two manoeuvre battalions to the El Mujahid Detachment in order for them to together attack along this axis, and this was sufficient forces on the basis of the decision taken by the division commander, who decided that the three units should be sufficient to attack along that axis. That's my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I ask you to slow down, Mr. Ribo. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Mr. Ribo, this brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. Thank you very much for taking the time to come and testify. You are now excused. You may stand down. Thank you very much, and travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Court will adjourn to tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 7th day of March, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24
